\section[dōśa]{\ml{ദോശ} (dōśa) — dosa}

\label{lesson:ML-C132-dosa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for vegetables, then the Malayalam for an onion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ദോശ}}
\textbf{\ml{ദോശ}} (\emph{dōśa}) — a thin rice pancake, often eaten at \textbf{\ml{പ്രാതൽ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A breakfast favourite.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dōśa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dōśa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dōśa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for vegetables, then the Malayalam for an onion, then say \emph{dōśa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ദോശ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dosa\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sāmpār]{\ml{സാമ്പാർ} (sāmpār) — sambar}

\label{lesson:ML-C132-sambar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an onion, then the Malayalam for dosa.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സാമ്പാർ}}
\textbf{\ml{സാമ്പാർ}} (\emph{sāmpār}) — a lentil and \textbf{\ml{പച്ചക്കറി}} stew, poured over rice or eaten with \textbf{\ml{ദോശ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What goes with dosa.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāmpār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāmpār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dōśayum sāmpārum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an onion, then the Malayalam for dosa, then say \emph{sāmpār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സാമ്പാർ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sambar\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[kaṟi]{\ml{കറി} (kaṟi) — a curry}

\label{lesson:ML-C132-curry}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for appam, then the Malayalam for puttu.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കറി}}
\textbf{\ml{കറി}} (\emph{kaṟi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a curry\textquotedblright{}, any dish that goes on rice. \textbf{\ml{മീൻ} \ml{കറി}} — \textquotedblleft{}fish curry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The word for what goes on rice.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṟi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṟi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mīn kaṟi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for appam, then the Malayalam for puttu, then say \emph{kaṟi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കറി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A curry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
